dehydrated_text:
Unfortunately, what happens is that over time because Jerusalem is so important and because the Jews believe they are special people who only worship the one true god, this will cause conflict with the Greeks. The Greeks, on the other hand, are very chauvinistic and proud people who believe their culture is superior. Many Jews will convert to the Hellenistic lifestyle, but this causes conflict and ultimately leads to something called the Maccabean revolt where a certain group of Jews decide to rebel against the Greeks. Even though they are a minority, because of their religious conviction and the will of God, they triumph and establish the Maccabean kingdom. This victory is celebrated today in Hanukkah, which commemorates the Maccabees' revolt against the Greeks.

The reason for this revolt was that the Greeks wanted Jews to celebrate their religion as well and tried to turn the Second Temple into a site to worship Greek gods. Fanatical Jews rebelled against this. However, the Maccabean kingdom does not last very long. Jerusalem being at the nexus of empires means the Romans will come and take control over the area. The Romans are even more chauvinistic and discriminatory towards the Jews, leading to three major wars between the Romans and the Jews. The entire Jewish diaspora revolts against the Romans, resulting in many Jews being massacred because the Romans are vicious. In 70 AD, they burn down the Second Temple to destroy the morale of the Jews. This destruction causes a shift in the Jewish religion. Remember that at this point, the Second Temple is a site of Jewish worship—this is where Yahweh lives. When the Second Temple is destroyed, many Jews choose to convert to Christianity as Paul created Christianity as a mechanism for Jews to still be Jews but also be Roman.

Those who stay become more fanatical and develop a very messianic eschatological attitude, meaning the end of the world is coming; God will destroy the Romans, and they must show their loyalty. They continue fighting even though they've lost the war against the Romans. They go into the Arabian desert where they incubate a new religion called Islam and prophesize the coming of the Messiah who turns out to be Muhammad.

At this point in history, Jews must leave Jerusalem because the Romans kicked them out. Their religion splinters into many different factions, with a major characteristic being that they've gone from temple worship to the worship of their law—Moses' law. The rabbis come into power; before it was the priests who controlled the temple. Now, it's the rabbis who are the Pharisees, those who teach the oral law of Moses, becoming the new elite in the Jewish diaspora.

Many Jews at this time convert to Christianity because early Christians were mostly Jews. Those who escape into the desert incubate Islam and eventually conquer the world, feeling they've achieved the messianic age by returning to Jerusalem where the Messiah will come, lead them to victory, bring all the Jews back, build the third temple, and usher in the messianic age.

This belief leads to the construction of the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, meant to be the third temple. Over time, it changes into a center of Islamic worship but was initially intended as the third temple. Many Jews convert to Islam because they believe Muhammad is the Messiah, while others settle throughout the world.
